name: zone38 authorized red-team audit (secret scanner / AI-code detector)
description: Authorized red-team audit of github.com/semanticRig/zone38 @ 60f42e2 (110 commits, full unshallowed history), an offline JS/TS secret scanner and AI-generated-code detector. Method: abductive engineering (abduction -> deduction -> induction) against the real CLI, read-only throughout. Question under test: can a real secret pass the CI gate without zone38 blocking it, and does zone38 deliver on its headline claim of detecting AI-generated code by mathematical structure (Shannon entropy / Index of Coincidence / Normalized Compression Distance)? Six of eleven investigated findings (INV-1..INV-11) were retained as forensically significant; the rest were CODE FACT/low-severity or open PLAUSIBLE hypotheses not executed. Reconstructed from audits/zone38/zone38_redteam_findings_2026-07-23.txt after the original case file referenced by the sealed bundle was never committed alongside it.

artifacts.description: INV-9 (HIGH) — 'Minified-skip' is a total detection bypass. runner.js:81-88: if record.surface.minified is true, the entire L05-L08 candidate pipeline is skipped (record.findings=[], record.review=[]); only URL analysis (L09) and regex rules (L10) run. Induction (poc-minified-bypass.js): NORMAL 29-line file with 25 regex-blind base64 secrets -> minified=false, 25 secrets reported, axis B=45, exit 1. Same content concatenated to one line (avgLineLen 1478) -> minified=true, 0 secrets reported, axis B=0, exit 0.

forensic_anomalies: Entropy pipeline is fully disabled by a one-line-length heuristic (minified=true)
Composed with regex-blind naming (d0..d24), this is a total secret-detection bypass, not a false-positive suppression edge case
On a minified file, zone38's secret detection collapses to regex-only -- the exact 'regex-based scanner' failure mode its own README criticizes
metadata.content_preview: runner.js:81-88 skips L05-L08 when surface.minified; poc-minified-bypass.js: 25 secrets/exit 1 (normal) vs 0 secrets/exit 0 (minified)

artifacts.description: INV-10 (Medium, CONFIRMED BY EVIDENCE) — the AI-slop detector is itself AI-agent-built; its thesis refutes itself. Objective git evidence: originally 'slopguard', 110 commits over 5 weeks, single author, feature/phase-N branches. History contains CLAUDE.md (Claude Code project instructions) and planner.instructions.md (phase-gated agent planner with explicit user-approval gating). .gitignore scrubs CLAUDE.md, PHASES.md, planner.instructions.md, solution/, solutionV2/ from the published tree. Scanning zone38 with itself yields axis A=9.2 'Minimal' (clears itself) while reporting 98 'secrets' at exit 0.

forensic_anomalies: AI coding agents were used in a human-directed, phase-gated workflow -- the 'written 100% by AI in one shot' framing is falsified by the 110-commit cadence
The decisive evidence of AI authorship lives in git history and gitignored planning files, outside the .js files the tool actually scans
zone38's core thesis (detect AI origin from code texture) is refuted by its own case: the ground truth here is procedural/historical, not textural
metadata.content_preview: 110 commits/5 weeks, CLAUDE.md + planner.instructions.md gitignored from published tree; self-scan axis A=9.2 'Minimal'

artifacts.description: INV-4 (Medium, CONFIRMED BY INDUCTION) — a purely representational change (hex vs base64/base32 encoding of the identical 32-byte secret) flips the CI decision inside a density window. icSignal is deterministically 0 for hex (IC ~0.064, above the 0.045 gate) and 1 for base64/base32. In the window N in [15,24] regex-blind secrets per file: base64 -> axis B>25 -> exit 1, hex -> exit 0, for the same underlying secret bytes. Existence result, not a universal bypass -- scoped to the density window.

forensic_anomalies: Same secret bytes, different textual representation, opposite CI decision inside N in [15,24]
NCD anti-correlates with the verdict: hex has the highest NCD (0.899, 'most alien') yet the weakest verdict, and NCD is not counted by the confirmation gate at all
metadata.content_preview: hex icSignal=0 (IC~0.064 > 0.045 gate) vs base64 icSignal=1; N in [15,24] flips exit 1 <-> exit 0 for identical secret bytes

artifacts.description: INV-2 (Medium, documentation integrity) — the real confirmation gate does not match the README's model. README claims all three signals (Shannon, IC, NCD) must agree before a secret is confirmed. CODE FACT: the real gate is L08.arbitrate -- HIGH requires effectivePipeline >= 0.65 AND >= 2 of {icSignal, ctfSignal, egsSpike, uniformity}; MEDIUM requires >= 0.50 AND >= 2. NCD is not among the four counted signals at all. Induction: secret#2 in hex is confirmed MEDIUM with icSignal=0 -- a secret confirmed without the IC signal, refuting 'all three must agree'.

forensic_anomalies: The user's mental model of the detector, built entirely from the README, does not match the actual implementation
NCD is described as one of three required signals but is not part of the real 4-signal counted gate at all
metadata.content_preview: L08.arbitrate: HIGH >=0.65 & >=2-of-4 signals, MEDIUM >=0.50 & >=2-of-4; NCD absent from the counted set despite README claim

artifacts.description: INV-11 (Medium, broken honest-degradation) — a 'Clean' verdict is emitted over 0 analyzed files. L13._aggregateProject returns {A:0,B:0,C:0} when perFile.length===0. zone38 only analyzes JS/TS; a repo with none yields 0 files -> axes all 0 -> verdict 'Clean'. There is no third not-analyzed/ABSTAIN state. Induction: five Python-only repos all produced analyzed=0, A=0 'Clean', exit 0 -- a CI running zone38 on a non-JS project gets an empty green that certifies nothing.

forensic_anomalies: Absence of analysis is reported identically to a genuinely clean result -- absence of a check surfaces as absence of a problem
No ABSTAIN/not-analyzed state exists in the verdict model, even though the tool's own conclusion elsewhere argues ABSTAIN is the epistemically honest posture for what it cannot actually measure
metadata.content_preview: perFile.length===0 -> {A:0,B:0,C:0} -> 'Clean'; reproduced on 5 Python-only repos, exit 0 every time

artifacts.source_tool: static reading of L13 axis B formula
artifacts.description: INV-8 (Medium) — detection is not blocking; axis B saturates low. L13 axis B = 0.45*findings + 0.25*patterns + 0.20*urls + 0.10*compression, each sub-score capped at 100; DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.B=25. Induction: a single detected hardcoded secret yields axis B ~10.6 -- reported (secrets=1) but exit 0. The gate is only crossed at ~15 base64 / ~25 hex secrets in one file; axis B saturates at ~45 even with 100 secrets (findings capped). Detection != blocking: the default gate tolerates a detected secret.

forensic_anomalies: A confirmed, reported secret finding does not by itself fail the CI gate at default thresholds
Axis B saturates well below 100 regardless of how many secrets are present, capping the maximum penalty a real leak can incur
metadata.content_preview: axis B = 0.45*findings+0.25*patterns+0.20*urls+0.10*compression; 1 secret -> B~10.6, exit 0; threshold B=25 crossed only at ~15-25 secrets/file

metadata.authorization: Authorized red-team audit against a public third-party tool, run from this repository as a VIGIA stress test.
metadata.reconstruction_note: This case file was referenced by ZONE38-REDTEAM-2026-07-23_bundle.json but never committed alongside it (2026-07-23, commit 0422884). Reconstructed 2026-07-24 from the full red-team findings .txt before that source file was removed. Field values (raw_score/prior_trust) are drawn from the 6 kept findings' documented severities; per-artifact acquisition_hash values are placeholders (no original per-artifact hashing was performed during the manual audit) and this file will NOT reproduce the original Evidence SHA-256 referenced in vigia_analysis_ZONE38_2026-07-23.md.
metadata.expected_verdict_rationale: Both prior verdicts on this case disagreed: the sealed VIGIA deterministic bundle recorded agent_verdict=NOISE at MINIMAL quality tier (confidence capped 3/5, submitted 1/1); a separate Claude/Cronos reasoning trace recorded INTENT at 75% confidence. Per CLAUDE.md's own verdict scale and Refutation Protocol, a MINIMAL-quality deterministic NOISE and an unrefuted single-source LLM narrative INTENT are not sufficient corroboration for a confirmed verdict either way. The findings' own conclusion states this explicitly: 'the honest posture toward such input is ABSTAIN, not a confident verdict.' expected_verdict is set to ABSTAIN accordingly, and cronos_audit_zone38_2026-07-23.md was annotated (not deleted) to record this as a stress-test case: an LLM narrative reasoning trace reached INTENT at 75% confidence without corroboration and without the Mandatory Refutation Protocol being applied -- illustrating how much an unfounded verdict is 'punished' by the Daubert-grade standard this project holds itself to.
